title: Slow the conversation down
summary: Use a warm tone, one short idea at a time, and extra response time. Listen for emotion, avoid correcting or arguing, and keep the person included and respected.

title: Offer two simple choices
summary: A yes-or-no question or two concrete options can be easier than an open-ended decision. Rephrase gently if the first question does not land.

title: Meet an accusation with reassurance
summary: A missing item can create fear and suspicion. Avoid taking the accusation personally or trying to win an argument; give a simple answer, reassure, and help search or shift attention.

title: Protect privacy during personal care
summary: Bathing may feel frightening, embarrassing, cold, or physically unpleasant. Prepare the room, explain each step, preserve covering and privacy, and let the person do what they can.

title: Reduce late-day overload
summary: For late-day restlessness, keep a familiar schedule, use daylight and appropriate activity earlier in the day, reduce clutter and noise, and offer a familiar calming activity.

title: Look for a reason behind distress
summary: Agitation often has a trigger. Consider pain, illness, fatigue, sensory strain, the environment, communication demands, and a sudden change that may need professional attention.

title: DICE: Describe
summary: Start with observable facts: what happened, when and where, who was present, what came before and after, and how distressing it was. Separate observation from interpretation.

title: DICE: Investigate
summary: Review possible contributors such as health or pain, sleep, senses, routine, communication, caregiver stress, culture, and the physical environment. Seek clinical help for medical concerns.

title: DICE: Create and evaluate
summary: Choose a small plan that supports comfort, clearer communication, meaningful activity, simpler tasks, and safety. Then observe whether it was practical and helpful, and adjust.

title: Act quickly when someone is missing
summary: Begin looking immediately and check nearby hazards and familiar destinations. If the person is not found within 15 minutes, call 911 and explain that the missing person has dementia.

title: Use human crisis support
summary: In the United States, call or text 988 for emotional distress or a suicide crisis. If there is immediate danger or urgent emergency assistance is needed, call 911 now.
